leading_positions.synthesis: Three members include base editing in their preferred configuration, but not the same one. Chabes and Linke propose a single-part prize for Liu, Komor and Gaudelli (cytosine and adenine base editors). Somfai includes B007 only as a second part for Liu alone, paired with B065 in a two-part prize. All three cite a defined deaminase chemistry and many independent replications. All three also name proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) priority question as reservations. They do not share a view on how many laureates the base-editing citation should name.

Aili and Aqvist both propose a single-part prize for Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli on targeted protein degradation by bifunctional molecules recruiting E3 ligases. Both name the missing approved degrader as a timing concern and both note that the cereblon molecular-glue line (Handa, Ito, Gray) would be left outside the three-name citation. They differ in emphasis: Aqvist weights breadth of ranking across all eight opening ballots, while Aili treats that breadth as acceptance and not as merit. No other member includes B011 in a preferred configuration, though Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai, Zou and Linke list it as an alternative or second choice.

Brzezinski alone proposes nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) on mechanistic grounds. He acknowledges that he cast the only first-place opening vote for it and that the N2 binding mode is unresolved. Dean and Ribbe are the named attribution risk.

Sparr alone proposes biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) as a physical-chemical organising principle. She names the in vivo relevance debate and the Pappu and Mittag attribution as open issues.

Zou alone proposes halide perovskite solar-cell absorbers (Miyasaka, Snaith, Park) as a distinct materials-chemistry achievement. She states that stability, lead content and the Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis attribution are unresolved, and that opening support for B047 was narrow.

Somfai alone proposes a two-part prize: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) plus base editing for Liu. He concedes that B065 had thin opening support and that the two parts share no unifying theme.

areas_of_agreement: No configuration is supported by a majority of five. Counting only explicit preferred configurations, B007 appears in three (one a Liu-only second part), B011 in two, and B028, B046, B047 and B065 in one each.
Every member names a specific, honestly stated weakness in their own first choice, and none claims a candidate is free of timing, attribution or scope objections.
Several members list B011 or B007 as an alternative: B011 is an alternative for Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai, Zou and Linke, and B007 is an alternative for Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Zou.
Each member reports no recusal-level conflict.
The three-laureate limit is stated by most members as a real constraint on B011, B028, B046, B047 and B007.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is a distinct chemical invention (deaminase engineering and directed evolution) or a successor step within the genome-editing story recognised in 2020.

Whether the chemically central B011 achievement is the bifunctional PROTAC design principle (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) or the molecular-glue and cereblon mechanism (Handa, Ito, Gray), and whether the two can be defined as one achievement.
Whether biomolecular condensation counts as chemistry and as a settled principle, given the open question of which cellular condensates are functional.
Whether the nitrogenase catalytic cycle is understood well enough to be cited as a mechanism, given the unresolved N2 binding mode.
Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a distinct achievement or an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
attribution_disputes: B007: Liu, Komor and Gaudelli versus the independent, near-contemporaneous Target-AID work of Kondo and Nishida; Somfai would name Liu alone, which leaves out the other four.
B011: Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli (bifunctional degraders) versus Handa, Ito and Gray (cereblon and molecular glues), with Sakamoto and Kim also credited on the shortlist.
B028: structure (Rees, Einsle) versus mechanism and biosynthesis (Seefeldt, Dean, Ribbe), with one seat contested at three names.
B046: Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag for credit on the multivalent and sequence-grammar framework.
B047: Miyasaka, Snaith and Park versus Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis, with the 2012 solid-state step shared.
B065: Buchwald and Hartwig versus Kosugi (and possibly Migita) for the earlier tin-amide work; Somfai flags this as not independently verified.
maturity_disputes: B011: no approved degrader is known to the members who raised this; Aqvist states he does not know the current regulatory status.
B007: clinical benefit is accumulating but long-term safety, bystander edits and off-target deamination are still being characterised.
B046: roughly fifteen years of work, but in vivo functional criteria are still debated.
B047: operational stability, lead content and scale-up are unresolved.
B028: the structures are confirmed by independent work, but the mechanism is open.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Aqvist: his work with Warshel and on free-energy and EVB simulation lies close to B026 and B018, which he ranks only as an alternative (B026); no recusal indicated for B011.
Sparr: field overlap with B058 (lipid nanoparticles) and B046 (phase behaviour), disclosed and not treated as grounds for recusal.
Aili: research overlap with Sparr on peptide-lipid and protein self-assembly, relevant to B046 only as a shared field.
Brzezinski and Zou: Stockholm University colleagues; described as collegial and not a recusal matter.
Linke, Somfai, Sparr: shared Lund affiliation among committee members; no shortlisted candidate is a Lund colleague or collaborator.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee frame base editing as distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and does it hold at three names (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) given Target-AID by Kondo and Nishida, or does Somfai's Liu-only option fit better?
Can PROTAC and molecular-glue contributions be separated into one defensible B011 citation, and which three of Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito and Gray would it name?
Does the absence of an approved degrader, as members understand it, make B011 premature, and what current regulatory evidence do members hold that bears on this?
Would members support a two-part prize, and if so, which pairing could share a three-laureate limit and be explained to a general audience?
For B046, can a citation reward the physical principle and founding experiments without endorsing contested cellular condensates, and would the other members regard it as chemistry?
For B028, is nitrogenase one attributable achievement or a line of work, and is the unresolved N2 binding mode a barrier to citing mechanism?
Which members who ranked B047 or B065 low would move if the citation or attribution were narrowed, and which not?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a split field: B007 has three explicit supporters across two different configurations, B011 has two, and four further candidates have one each. All eight members agree on how to describe the main reservations (CRISPR proximity, Target-AID priority, missing degrader approval, glue attribution), so round 2 mostly turns on weighting these, not on discovering new objections.
